chunks: And al-Shaykh, may Allah تعالى support him, informed me with this chain from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Sālim, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar, who said:

I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: May I be made your ransom, what do you say regarding a woman who is on a journey with men among whom she has no maḥram, and there is no woman with them, then the woman dies—what is to be done with her? He said: “From her, that which Allah has made subject to tayammum is washed, and she is not touched, nor is anything of her beauties uncovered which Allah has commanded to be concealed.” I said: Then how is that to be done with her? He said: “The inside of her palms is washed, then the outside of her palms is washed.”
As for the report narrated by Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from Dāwūd ibn Sirḥān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

Concerning a man who dies on a journey or in a land where there are only women with him, he said: “He is buried and not given ghusl.” What is meant by this is when he is naked: he is buried and not given ghusl. But if he has some clothing on him, then his ghusl is unavoidable; water is poured over him without touching any part of his limbs, according to what we have mentioned.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah تعالى support him, said: If a woman dies while there is in her womb a living child that is moving, her abdomen is cut from her left side, the child is taken out from it, then the place is sewn up, and afterward she is given ghusl, shrouded, perfumed with ḥunūṭ, and buried. And if the child dies in her womb while she is alive, the midwife, or one who takes her place in managing the woman’s affair, inserts her hand into her private part and removes the dead child from it. If she cannot remove it intact, she cuts it up and removes it in pieces, and it is given ghusl, shrouded, perfumed with ḥunūṭ, then buried.

key_terms.التَّيَمُّمَ: dry ablution; here indicating the body parts treated in a limited washing procedure
key_terms.الْقَابِلَةُ: the midwife who manages childbirth-related procedures
key_terms.عُرْيَانًا: naked, without clothing covering the body
key_terms.مَحَاسِنِهَا: the parts of her beauty that must remain covered
key_terms.يُغْسَلُ: is washed ritually in preparation for burial

ai.seo_question: What are the Shia rulings on washing and burying a deceased person when only the opposite gender is present?
ai.summary: This text gives fiqh rulings for handling the dead when normal gender-appropriate washing is not possible during travel or isolation. It emphasizes preserving modesty, avoiding unlawful touching, and outlines procedures for exceptional cases involving deceased pregnant women or a dead fetus.
